source_notes.note: The registered source is arXiv:2206.13668v4, marked19 Mar2024. Its title says components (plural), whereas the corpus metadata says component. Main text and acknowledgements end on PDF page21 before references at y580.205; evidence is clipped at y572. No appendix or S-prefixed supplementary passage is imported.

The Q transformations in the algebraic conclusions range over O(d), as specified by the preceding setting and G_T definition. They are not arbitrary invertible matrices: diagonal rescalings would otherwise invalidate the conclusion. A maps Y to epsilon, and the surviving ambiguity is left multiplication by signed permutations, changing rows rather than columns.

Equation(10) defines G_T(V) as a subset of O(d), but the following source sentence calls it a subset of Omega, which contains QA. Proposition4.1 gives the actual parameter set Omega_0={QA:Q in G_T(V)}. Preserve the original sentence while keeping transformations Q separate from parameter matrices QA. G_T is not generally a group or the stabilizer of T.

Theorems5.3/5.10 concern arbitrary symmetric tensors, not necessarily realizable as moments/cumulants of a distribution. Theorems5.5/5.14 concern model(1) with centered unit-covariance hidden components and a chosen h_r. No observational-model premise or generating-function existence condition is imported into the algebraic theorems.

h_r denotes either the order-r raw moment tensor or the order-r classical cumulant tensor. Listing both definitions resolves a notation alternative, not a conjunction requiring both tensors to satisfy the restrictions. Their higher-order entries differ; zero mean makes only the third-order tensors coincide. Remark3.1’s extensions are not folded into the default definition.

The source defines moments by expectations and also derivatives of the MGF, and cumulants through log-MGF derivatives. It does not specify a neighborhood where the MGF is finite or analytic. Theorems require the indicated tensors to exist, but finite moments of one order alone do not establish that analytic representation. Preserve this unresolved regularity convention; do not silently assume all moments or replace the original cumulant definition.

For r≥3, Theorem5.3 requires at least d−1 nonzero full diagonal entries, equivalently at most one zero. Its r=2 branch needs pairwise distinct matrix diagonals. For reflectional tensors, condition(14) compares repeated-pair contractions summed over all indices, not just full diagonal entries. These conditions are neither interchangeable nor part of the entrywise zero-pattern definitions.

Definition5.8 permits only the zero tensor at odd order. Theorem5.10 takes even r and l=(r−2)/2, with the standard positive-order context; r=2 yields an empty contraction and distinct diagonal entries. Theorem5.14 does not explicitly exclude r=2, but h_2(epsilon)=I_d under its normalization, so genericity fails for d>1. No new lower bound on r is inserted into the source statement.

Reflectionally invariant means every potentially nonzero entry has even multiplicity of each coordinate label, including off-diagonal pair patterns. It does not mean invariant under every orthogonal transformation. Theorem5.10 describes all transformations into the entire reflectional space, yielding signed permutations; Lemma5.13 describes the smaller exact stabilizer of a fixed generic tensor. The two sets are not merged.

The statistical conclusions determine A from the population distribution up to row sign/permutation, not exact recovery of a unique orientation, a finite-sample estimator or a convergence rate. Neither diagonal constraints at one selected order nor reflectional constraints imply independence. Corollaries for common-variance, elliptical or mean-independent models and later minimum-distance estimation results are not extra Theorems or premises of the general identification statements.

T5.3.domain: T is an arbitrary real symmetric order-r tensor; Q ranges over O(d) under the standing transformation convention.

branches.higher_order: r≥3, diagonal T with at least d−1 nonzero full diagonal entries.
branches.second_order: r=2 with pairwise distinct diagonal entries; preserve this separate branch.

T5.3.conclusion: All orthogonal Q taking T into the diagonal space are exactly signed permutations; G_T(Vdiag)=SP(d). No distributional realizability assumption.

T5.5.model: AY=epsilon, invertible A, observed Y, hidden centered epsilon with covariance I_d.
T5.5.choice: Some fixed r≥3 and either h_r=mu_r or h_r=kappa_r, diagonal with at most one zero full diagonal entry.
T5.5.conclusion: Population identification of A up to left signed-permutation action, hence row permutations and row signs. Independence and non-Gaussian-component assumptions are not separately imposed.

T5.10.domain: Arbitrary symmetric reflectionally invariant tensor at even positive order r; Q in O(d).
T5.10.local_binders: l=(r−2)/2; each i_a sums over[d], and j,k range over[d] with j≠k. Condition(14) is bound inline and separately archived as D13 for reuse by Theorem5.14.
T5.10.conclusion: G_T(Vrefl)=SP(d), not a claim that the exact stabilizer Q*T=T is all of SP(d).

T5.14.model: Same observed normalized linear model as Theorem5.5.
T5.14.choice: For some even r, the chosen h_r(epsilon) is reflectionally invariant and satisfies the repeated-pair contraction condition(14). Moments and cumulants are alternatives.
T5.14.conclusion: A is identifiable up to row signs and permutations. The statement does not invoke independence or require a specific generative component model.
T5.14.order_note: The original statement says even r; the normalized second-order case cannot satisfy condition(14) for d>1.
